newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says no alternative to public spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says no alternative to public spending cuts.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Monday there was no alternative to unpopular public spending cuts and urged his government to stay the course and do a better job at explaining its policies.

Chirac used a speech to an audience of 3,000 in northern France to make a strong defence of Prime Minister Alain Juppe's embattled centre-right government on a day when most school teachers staged a one-day strike to protest at job cuts.
"There are perfectly understandable doubts and perfectly legitimate impatience...But the right decisions have been taken and, I am telling you, perseverance will pay off," he said.
Chirac sought to rebutt criticism of the government within his conservative coalition and in public opinion, saying France had to manage its finances seriously.

"The government is doing that, but much remains to be done to make public spending efficient and to make savings wherever possible. This discipline is not always popular, but there is no other way," he said.
On one of his regular grassroots visits to provincial France, Chirac said the government lacked neither determination nor consistency but needed to remember the need to explain policy clearly.
It was the second time in a week that he had come to the defence of Juppe, who has called a parliamentary confidence vote on Wednesday to try to unite his fractious coalition.
The head of state intervened personally last week to silence anti-Juppe sniping by legislators in their Gaullist RPR party.

Two dissident members of the coalition announced on Monday they would not vote confidence in the government. But since the conservative parties have a four-fifths majority in the National Assembly, there was no risk of a defeat.
Both defectors, Jean-Louis Beaumont and Bruno Retailleau, are members of the junior coalition parnter, the Union for French Democracy (UDF).
